claims.text: Mild pre-oxidation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating will form a thin, continuous, coherent Cu- and Fe-rich oxide layer.
The Cu- and Fe-rich oxide layer will be lubricious.
The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a uniform phase distribution.
Post-deposition annealing in a mildly oxidative atmosphere can deliberately produce the proposed oxide layer.
At 500–800°C, sliding-induced mechanical deformation is active.
At 500–800°C, thermal oxidation is sufficiently active to form or sustain the proposed protective oxide layer.
The oxide layer acts as a solid lubricant and thereby lowers friction during high-temperature sliding.
The oxide layer acts as a barrier that minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reducing direct metal-to-metal contact will reduce adhesive wear.
The oxide layer will moderate localized damage and microcrack formation during high-temperature sliding.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have a statistically significant reduction in wear depth relative to untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have a statistically significant reduction in coefficient of friction relative to untreated coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will exhibit more uniform microscopic deformation patterns than untreated coatings.
The predicted mechanism should hold within 500–800°C but may change outside that temperature window because oxidation dynamics differ.
Secondary microstructural changes during sliding may interact with the oxide layer.

contradictions.description: The intervention and structural-mediator fields describe the oxide as formed before sliding by pre-oxidation, whereas the mechanism calls it 'in situ formed' and the boundary implies that operating-temperature oxidation kinetics form the protective layer. It is therefore unclear whether the operative mediator is pre-existing, generated during sliding, or both.
